findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued is frozen at import time
findings.body: queued is declared as queued: datetime = timezone.now() on the dataclass. That expression is evaluated once when the class body runs, not when an instance is created. Every AssignmentSource.from_integration() call on the inbound webhook path therefore stores the same timestamp: the moment this module was first imported in the process. Long-lived web and worker processes make that value hours or days old, so the field cannot distinguish or order the rapid successive assignee changes this PR is about. Dataclass equality includes queued, so distinct events for the same integration also compare equal for the life of the process, and to_dict() writes that stale timestamp into every sync_assignee_outbound payload. This needs field(default_factory=timezone.now). The new test only checks that queued is not None, so it does not catch the shared value.

findings.title: to_dict() embeds a datetime in Celery task kwargs
findings.body: to_dict() returns asdict(self), so queued is a raw datetime. sync_group_assignee_outbound passes that dict straight to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async as assignment_source_dict. A JSON task transport (Celery JSON serializer, or Sentry taskworker) cannot encode datetime and raises TypeError while enqueueing. That apply_async call is synchronous inside GroupAssignee.assign and deassign, so an inbound webhook can persist the assignee and then fail, and the change is never pushed to any other integration. from_dict only does cls(**input_dict) inside a ValueError/TypeError handler and does not parse ISO-8601 strings. If a serializer stringifies the timestamp, queued is left as a string; if construction raises, from_dict returns None. The outbound task treats a None source as "not an echo" and performs the sync anyway, which brings the assignee loop back. self.tasks() runs eagerly and does not round-trip the serializer, and no test calls from_dict(source.to_dict()), so CI will not catch this.

findings.title: Echo guard drops every linked issue on the source integration
findings.body: should_sync returns False for the entire integration whenever sync_source.integration_id matches org_integration.integration_id. AssignmentSource does not record the external issue key, and sync_group_assignee_outbound attaches that same source to every GroupLink on the Sentry issue. A group may be linked to multiple external issues on one integration; GroupLink uniqueness is on the external-issue id, not the integration. An assignee webhook from Jira ticket A therefore skips outbound sync for ticket A and also for ticket B on the same Jira integration, so ticket B's assignee stays stale even with outbound assignee sync enabled. sync_group_assignee_inbound already has external_issue_key, and the outbound task already loads the target ExternalIssue, so the guard should skip only the originating issue. Skipping that one key still stops the echo; GroupAssignee.assign does not enqueue outbound sync when the assignee is unchanged, so a follow-up webhook that maps to the same Sentry user will not bounce.

findings.title: Inbound wiring and cross-integration sync are untested
findings.body: The new test calls GroupAssignee.objects.assign directly with an AssignmentSource and only covers the matching-integration assign case. test_assignee_sync_inbound_assign and test_assignee_sync_inbound_deassign call sync_group_assignee_inbound, which is the production webhook entry point that must pass assignment_source into assign and deassign, but they never assert that outbound sync to the source integration is skipped. Removing those assignment_source= arguments in sync.py would leave both inbound tests green and restore the loop. There is also no test that a second integration still receives the outbound update, and no test that deassign with a matching source skips outbound (test_assignee_sync_outbound_unassign still expects assignment_source=None). A guard that dropped every sourced sync, or a deassign path that forgot the source, would pass CI.
